chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who gives food to the miller, making a contract that he gives the owner twelve qirats for every ten [units], and he said, 'No.' I said, 'And a man gives simsim (sesame) to the presser and guarantees him a specified number of artals for every sa', and he said, 'No.'

key_terms.يُقَاطِعُهُ: he makes a contract/agreement with him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on guaranteeing a fixed amount of flour for a specific amount of grain in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the application of *gharar* (uncertainty) in *muqata'ah* contracts, where the Imam rejects guaranteeing a fixed output (12 dirhams of flour for 10 units of grain) because the actual yield depends on variable factors like milling efficiency. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinguishes between permissible processing fees and impermissible fixed-guarantee exchanges, emphasizing that the risk of yield fluctuation must remain with the owner of the raw material. The ruling underscores the principle that when the quantity of the processed good is not known at the time of contract, it introduces excessive uncertainty invalidating the exchange.
